premises.text: Once a Web3 game has traction, its economy becomes a real economy that can crash without Fed-like management
premises.evidence_span: as soon as you have a game that has like some amount of traction on web 3, your biggest problem is how do I make sure my economy doesn't crash? How do I keep the economy healthy?

premises.text: Healthy economies require that participants can produce and that taxes create currency value
premises.evidence_span: The first principle is that the people who are participating in the economy should be able to produce in that economy. And the second principle is that there should be, you know, taxes create value

premises.text: Platform offers on-chain minigames, crafting, activity rewards, healthy-behavior leaderboards, and security bots
premises.evidence_span: we have on-chain minigames, on-chain crafting, Minecraft style. We allow games to deliver rewards to their players for activities that they do. We have leaderboards that incentivize players to act in a healthy manner inside the economy. And we run security bots as well to make sure that the economy is protected against bad actors

premises.text: Charge $1000/month for on-chain economy visibility and $0.10 per user interaction as infrastructure
premises.evidence_span: we charge $1,000 per month to anyone who wants to know what's going on in an on-chain economy. And then for game projects, we charge as an infrastructure provider. We charge them $0.10 per interactions that their users make against our platform, against our smart contracts and our APIs

value.text: Keep Web3 game economies healthy and prevent crashes
value.evidence_span: how do I make sure my economy doesn't crash? How do I keep the economy healthy? And that's the problem that we help games to solve

causal_links.evidence_span: features on our platform that help games maintain healthy economies

notes: Feature list (minigames/crafting/rewards/leaderboards/bots) treated as one economy-tooling mechanism (§4.1.2). Price tiers kept as one commercial premise (§4.1.3). Volume metrics excluded.
